# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verifier integrity gate (gh-1579) — classify harbor verifier stdout.

A harbor trial's verifier can silently skip work: the filter-js-from-html
verifier drives 439 XSS vectors through a real Chrome in 28 batches, and
when a batch page fails to load (chromedriver read timeout / connection
refused) the batch's vectors are silently skipped and implicitly counted
as blocked — while the test still prints its success claim. The scorer
that only reads `rewards` then trusts a lie.

This module is the named protocol every trust decision about a verifier
verdict passes through: ``classify(stdout_text) -> IntegrityVerdict``.
It is PURE — stdout text in, a structured verdict out, no IO, no eval,
no shell, no template rendering of captured groups (verifier stdout is
task-influenced output: data, never instructions). The file read lives in
``read_stdout`` (called from summary._trial_rows); captured log text is
length-capped before it leaves this module, and report lines built from a
verdict quote only batch/skip metadata, never raw log blobs.

Signals (the core set):

- S1 ``FailedLoad`` — a ``Failed to load URL: HTTPConnectionPool(...):
  Read timed out|Connection refused|ConnectionResetError`` line, bound to
  the preceding ``RUN BATCH N (contains K tests)`` header (batch id +
  skipped-test count). A failure seen before any header binds to no
  batch (batch=None, E1) and contributes 0 to ``skipped_tests``. One
  signal per batch (repeat failures in the same batch count once).
- S2 ``RetryStorm`` — urllib3 ``Retrying (...)`` / ``ConnectionResetError``
  churn. At/above ``RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD`` alone it downgrades the
  verdict to ``suspect`` (annotation only, never a score change); the
  threshold is calibrated above the clean siblings' handful of retries.
- S3 ``SuccessClaim`` — a ``✓ ... blocked all N ...`` summary line
  captured verbatim (length-capped). Only a signal when S1 fired in the
  same stdout (E6): the claim contradicts the failed loads — the lie
  marker. A lone success line is the normal clean case.

Statuses:

- ``ok``          — no S1, S2 below threshold; the verdict stands.
- ``suspect``     — S2 alone at/above threshold; annotated, score stands.
- ``compromised`` — S1 fired; the verdict is untrusted (I1: a trial in
  this state can never count as resolved).
- ``unreadable``  — stdout absent/blank/undecodable (I2: absence of
  evidence is reported, never assumed clean; a pass may still score, but
  the report flags that the gate could not inspect it).

The detector matches patterns, not task names (I3): the same failure mode
in any browser/HTTP-driven verifier of any family is caught. Patterns are
bounded literal+simple-regex matches over a line stream — no nested
quantifiers, no backreferences — so a 100 MB stdout parses in linear
time (UT-4 pins the bound).

Upstream escalation (the task-side fix, fail-or-retry instead of a
silent skip): harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2#89.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

OK = "ok"
SUSPECT = "suspect"
COMPROMISED = "compromised"
UNREADABLE = "unreadable"

# E3: retry/connection churn below this many events leaves the verdict
# ok — the clean sibling trials log a handful of retries and must stay
# quiet; the incident run logged 84. Named constant, pinned by UT-3.
RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD = 20

# Captured log text is length-capped before it enters any verdict/report.
_MAX_CLAIM_CHARS = 200

_BATCH_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"RUN BATCH (\d+) \(contains (\d+) tests\)")
# E8: bound to the full driver-failure shape, never the bare "Failed to
# load URL" substring (a task about error pages must not trip the gate).
_FAILED_LOAD_RE = re.compile(
    r"Failed to load URL: HTTPConnectionPool\([^)]*\): "
    r"(?:Read timed out|Connection refused|ConnectionResetError)"
)
_RETRY_RE = re.compile(r"Retrying \(")
_RESET_RE = re.compile(r"ConnectionResetError")
_CLAIM_RE = re.compile(r"✓.*\bblocked all (\d+)\b")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FailedLoad:
    """S1: a page the verifier failed to load — its tests never ran."""

    batch: int | None  # None = seen before any RUN BATCH header (E1)
    n_tests: int | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RetryStorm:
    """S2: urllib3 retry/connection churn (annotation-grade on its own)."""

    count: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SuccessClaim:
    """S3: the success claim line, verbatim (length-capped) — a lie marker
    only when a FailedLoad fired in the same stdout (E6)."""

    claim: str
    total_tests: int | None


Signal = FailedLoad | RetryStorm | SuccessClaim


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IntegrityVerdict:
    """The structured trust verdict for one verifier stdout."""

    status: str  # OK | SUSPECT | COMPROMISED | UNREADABLE
    signals: tuple[Signal, ...]
    skipped_tests: int | None  # batch-bound skips; None when no S1 fired
    total_tests: int | None = None  # claimed/header-declared vector total

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """Report-grade detail: batches + skip counts only — never raw log
        text (report lines quote metadata, not blobs)."""
        loads = [s for s in self.signals if isinstance(s, FailedLoad)]
        batches = [
            "unknown" if s.batch is None else str(s.batch) for s in loads
        ]
        batch_part = f"batches {','.join(batches)} skipped"
        skips = self.skipped_tests or 0
        if skips and self.total_tests:
            skip_part = f"{skips}/{self.total_tests} vectors never ran"
        elif skips:
            skip_part = f"{skips} vectors never ran"
        else:
            # Unknown-bindings contribute 0 (E1): no attributable skips.
            skip_part = "skipped-test count unknown"
        return f"{batch_part} — {skip_part}"


def classify(stdout_text: str | None) -> IntegrityVerdict:
    """Classify one verifier's stdout (pure; None = absent/undecodable)."""
    if stdout_text is None or "\x00" in stdout_text or not stdout_text.strip():
        # I2, fail-closed: absent, blank, or binary garbage is unreadable —
        # never silently ok on a pass.
        return IntegrityVerdict(UNREADABLE, (), None, None)

    loads: list[FailedLoad] = []
    seen_batches: set[int] = set()
    current: tuple[int, int] | None = None  # (batch id, n tests)
    retry_count = 0
    claim: SuccessClaim | None = None
    header_total = 0

    for line in stdout_text.splitlines():
        header = _BATCH_HEADER_RE.search(line)
        if header:
            current = (int(header.group(1)), int(header.group(2)))
            header_total += current[1]
            continue
        if _FAILED_LOAD_RE.search(line):
            if current is None:
                # E1: outside any batch — kept, but never misattributed.
                loads.append(FailedLoad(None, None))
            elif current[0] not in seen_batches:
                loads.append(FailedLoad(current[0], current[1]))
                seen_batches.add(current[0])
            continue
        if _RETRY_RE.search(line) or _RESET_RE.search(line):
            retry_count += 1
            continue
        if claim is None:
            match = _CLAIM_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                claim = SuccessClaim(
                    line.strip()[:_MAX_CLAIM_CHARS], int(match.group(1))
                )

    signals: list[Signal] = list(loads)
    skipped_tests: int | None = None
    total_tests: int | None = None
    if loads:
        skipped_tests = sum(s.n_tests or 0 for s in loads if s.batch is not None)
        total_tests = claim.total_tests if claim else (header_total or None)
        if claim is not None:
            signals.append(claim)  # S3 requires S1 (E6)
    elif claim is not None:
        total_tests = claim.total_tests
    if retry_count >= RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD:
        signals.append(RetryStorm(retry_count))

    if loads:
        status = COMPROMISED
    elif retry_count >= RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD:
        status = SUSPECT
    else:
        status = OK
    return IntegrityVerdict(status, tuple(signals), skipped_tests, total_tests)

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
    session logs, in file then line order."""
    ledgers = []
    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
            try:
                text = path.read_text()
            except OSError:
                continue
            for line in text.splitlines():
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    record = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue
                if (
                    isinstance(record, dict)
                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
                ):
                    ledgers.append(record)
    return ledgers


_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")  # keep in lockstep with the Dart
# `TaskLedgerItemStatus` enum and the SIBLING copy in
# bench/terminal_bench/summary.py (the two summary scripts are
# standalone-by-design — different layout roots — so this parser is
# duplicated; change both together).


def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
    when the session carries no ledger.

    Tolerates the corrupt payloads the Dart fold deliberately tolerates
    ("a corrupt ledger payload never throws"): a non-dict `data`, or an
    `items` that is not a list, degrades to `checklist: none` — never an
    AttributeError. An items-less ledger is `none` too: it verifies
    nothing, and rendering 0/0 would count it as fully verified in the
    coverage tally below. Duplicate of the sibling parser in
    bench/terminal_bench/summary.py (the scripts are standalone-by-design)
    — change both together.
    """
    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
    if not ledgers:
        return "checklist: none"
    data = ledgers[-1].get("data")
    rows = data.get("items") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    items = rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []
    if not items:
        return "checklist: none"
    total = len(items)
    verified = sum(
        1
        for item in items
        if isinstance(item, dict)
        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
    )
    unmet = total - verified
    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
    if unmet:
        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
    return cell


def _status(row: dict) -> str:
    """The row's integrity status (gh-1579). Rows that predate the gate
    (hand-built splits) count as ok — the gate is additive (AC8)."""
    verdict = row.get("integrity")
    return verdict.status if verdict is not None else "ok"


def _trial_rows(job_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
    # gh-1579: the integrity gate rides the same lazy-import pattern as
    # families below — importlib-based harnesses load this module
    # without this dir on sys.path.
    import verifier_integrity as vi

    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(str(job_dir / "*" / "result.json"))):
        data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
        rewards = (data.get("verifier_result") or {}).get("rewards") or {}
        scores = [float(v) for v in rewards.values()]
        resolved = bool(scores) and all(v >= 1.0 for v in scores)
        exception = (data.get("exception_info") or {}).get("exception_type") or ""
        # Issue #1123: token/cost accounting folded in by fa_agent.py at
        # populate_context_post_run time; absent (old runs) → zeros + n/a.
        agent = data.get("agent_result") or {}
        metadata = agent.get("metadata") or {}
        trial_dir = Path(path).parent
        # gh-1579 integrity gate: read + classify the verifier's stdout
        # BEFORE the verdict is trusted (pure classifier; IO here).
        stdout_text, stdout_reason = vi.read_stdout(trial_dir)
        verdict = vi.classify(stdout_text)
        if verdict.status == vi.COMPROMISED:
            note = verdict.describe()
        elif verdict.status == vi.SUSPECT:
            storms = [
                s.count for s in verdict.signals if isinstance(s, vi.RetryStorm)
            ]
            note = f"{storms[0]} retry/connection warnings"
        elif verdict.status == vi.UNREADABLE:
            note = f"stdout {stdout_reason}"
        else:
            note = ""
        rows.append({
            "resolved": resolved,
            "exception": exception,
            "tokens_in": agent.get("n_input_tokens") or 0,
            "tokens_out": agent.get("n_output_tokens") or 0,
            "cost": agent.get("cost_usd"),
            "estimated": metadata.get("estimated_tokens") or 0,
            "checklist": _ledger_cell(trial_dir),
            "trial": f"{job_dir.name}/{trial_dir.name}",
            "integrity": verdict,
            "integrity_note": note,
        })
    return rows


def render(splits: dict, expected=None, title=None, ledger=None, run_label=None):
    """Build the summary (lines, problems) — pure, testable.

    title: report heading (family mode, issue #1124); defaults to the
    legacy 4.0 heading. ledger: dict(dataset=, model=, fa_ref=, run_url=)
    — when set, a paste-ready per-version results-ledger row is appended
    with the real cost totals computed below (issue #1124 + #1123).
    run_label: provider+model tag (gh-1503, BENCH_RUN_LABEL env) so glm
    and kimi runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
    """
    lines = [title or "### fa on Terminal-Bench 4.0", ""]
    problems: list[str] = []
    if run_label:
        # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model (BENCH_RUN_LABEL,
        # set by bench-harbor.yml's provider resolve step — the same
        # contract bench.yml's gh-1471 summary uses).
        lines.append(f"Provider: {run_label} (gh-1503).")
    has_jobs = any(rows for rows in splits.values())

    if not has_jobs:
        lines.append("**No harbor jobs found — the run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no harbor jobs found")
        return lines, problems

    total_resolved = total_rows = 0
    total_attempted = 0
    total_scored = 0
    total_compromised = 0
    compromised_entries: list[str] = []
    suspect_entries: list[str] = []
    unreadable_entries: list[str] = []
    total_in = total_out = total_est = 0
    costs: list[float] = []
    unpriced = 0
    table = [
        "| split | resolved | rate | tokens in/out | est cost |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for split, label in (("cpu", "CPU shards"), ("gpu", "GPU shards")):
        rows = splits[split]
        if not rows:
            table.append(f"| {label} | 0/0 | no trials | — | n/a |")
            continue
        # gh-1556 AC3: presence counts — every trial that produced a
        # readable result.json attempted the task; the errored subset is
        # scored separately below (it errored before a verdict).
        total_attempted += len(rows)
        scored = [r for r in rows if not r["exception"]]
        errored = len(rows) - len(scored)
        # gh-1579 integrity gate (I1): a compromised verifier run is a
        # class of its own — pulled out of the scored pool entirely
        # (neither the resolved numerator nor the clean denominator — a
        # compromised pass poisons the rate if scored, and hiding it
        # lies by omission), reported by name in its own breakdown.
        comp = [r for r in scored if _status(r) == "compromised"]
        trusted = [r for r in scored if _status(r) != "compromised"]
        resolved = sum(1 for r in trusted if r["resolved"])
        total_resolved += resolved
        total_rows += len(trusted)
        total_scored += len(scored)
        total_compromised += len(comp)
        rate = f"{resolved / len(trusted):.1%}" if trusted else None
        if errored and not comp:
            note = f"{errored} errored"
        elif comp:
            parts = ([rate] if rate else []) + [f"{len(comp)} verifier-compromised"]
            if errored:
                parts.append(f"{errored} errored")
            note = "; ".join(parts)
        else:
            note = rate or "no trials"
        split_in = sum(r["tokens_in"] for r in scored)
        split_out = sum(r["tokens_out"] for r in scored)
        split_costs = [r["cost"] for r in scored if r["cost"] is not None]
        unpriced += sum(1 for r in scored if r["tokens_in"] and r["cost"] is None)
        costs.extend(split_costs)
        total_in += split_in
        total_out += split_out
        total_est += sum(r["estimated"] for r in scored)
        cost_cell = f"${sum(split_costs):.4f}" if split_costs else "n/a"
        table.append(
            f"| {label} | {resolved}/{len(trusted)} | {note} | {split_in}/{split_out} | {cost_cell} |"
        )
        # gh-1579: per-trial integrity entries across all classes; the
        # compromised breakdown lists errored trials too (E7 — post-
        # mortems see the poisoned stdout even when scoring ignored it),
        # the unreadable flag is pass-only (I2), suspect annotates only.
        for r in rows:
            status = _status(r)
            if status == "compromised":
                compromised_entries.append(f"{r['trial']} ({r['integrity_note']})")
            elif status == "suspect":
                suspect_entries.append(f"{r['trial']} ({r['integrity_note']})")
            elif (
                status == "unreadable"
                and r["resolved"]
                and not r["exception"]
            ):
                unreadable_entries.append(f"{r['trial']} ({r['integrity_note']})")
    lines.append(f"**Resolution: {total_resolved}/{total_rows} scored trials**")
    if total_attempted != total_rows:
        bits = []
        errored_total = total_attempted - total_scored
        if errored_total:
            bits.append(
                f"{errored_total} errored before a verdict — see the errored breakdown below"
            )
        if total_compromised:
            bits.append(
                f"{total_compromised} verifier-compromised (verdict untrusted)"
                " — see the integrity breakdown below"
            )
        lines.append(
            f"**Attempted: {total_attempted} trials produced a result.json "
            f"({'; '.join(bits)})**"
        )
    if total_in or total_out:
        cost_total = f"${sum(costs):.4f}" if costs else "n/a"
        suffix = f" — {unpriced} trial(s) unpriced (model missing from pricing.json)" if unpriced else ""
        lines.append(f"**Spend: {cost_total} — tokens in/out: {total_in}/{total_out}{suffix}**")
        if total_est:
            lines.append(
                f"includes ~{total_est} estimated tokens (chars/4 where the provider omitted usage)"
            )
    lines.append("")
    lines.extend(table)

    # gh-1412: near-miss proximity — per-trial checklist coverage from the
    # hidden `task_ledger` records the FinalizeGate contract emits. Only
    # trials WITH a ledger speak here (legacy runs stay silent), and the
    # block lists the incomplete ones by name: "failed 1 of 7 checks,
    # checklist verified 6" is the diagnostic the card exists for.
    ledgered = [
        (r["trial"], r["checklist"])
        for rows in splits.values()
        for r in rows
        if r["checklist"] != "checklist: none"
    ]
    if ledgered:
        fully = sum(1 for _, cell in ledgered if " unmet" not in cell)
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            f"Checklist coverage (gh-1412): {fully}/{len(ledgered)}"
            " ledgered trials fully verified"
        )
        for trial, cell in sorted(ledgered):
            if " unmet" in cell:
                lines.append(f"- {trial}: {cell}")

    exceptions: dict[str, int] = {}
    for rows in splits.values():
        for r in rows:
            if r["exception"]:
                exceptions[r["exception"]] = exceptions.get(r["exception"], 0) + 1
    if exceptions:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            "Errored trials (harness/infra failure, not scored): "
            + ", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in sorted(exceptions.items()))
        )
        # gh-1556 AC3: the errored class is REPORTED (breakdown line
        # above), never a verdict — its trials produced a result.json, so
        # the lost-shard guard below (presence-counted) keeps its teeth
        # only for genuinely missing trials.

    # gh-1579: the integrity-gate breakdowns, next to the errored-class
    # line (report, don't redden — none of the three lines touches the
    # exit code; only the completeness guard below can).
    if compromised_entries:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            "Verifier-compromised trials (verdict untrusted, excluded from "
            "resolution): "
            + ", ".join(compromised_entries)
            + f" ×{len(compromised_entries)}"
        )
    if suspect_entries:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            "Verifier-suspect trials (retry/connection storm — annotated, "
            "verdict stands): "
            + ", ".join(suspect_entries)
            + f" ×{len(suspect_entries)}"
        )
    if unreadable_entries:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            "Verifier-unreadable trials (no readable verifier stdout — pass "
            "not gate-checked): "
            + ", ".join(unreadable_entries)
            + f" ×{len(unreadable_entries)}"
        )

    if expected is not None and total_attempted < expected:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            f"**Incomplete run: {total_attempted}/{expected} expected trials attempted"
            " (lost or timed-out shard).**"
        )
        problems.append(f"only {total_attempted}/{expected} expected trials attempted")

    if ledger:
        rate = f"{total_resolved / total_rows:.1%}" if total_rows else "no trials"
        cost_cell = f"${sum(costs):.4f}" if costs else "n/a"
        date = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
        lines += [
            "",
            "### Ledger row — append to docs/bench.md (rows are append-only)",
            "",
            "| dataset | model | fa | date | resolution | cost | run |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
            f"| {ledger['dataset']} | {ledger['model']} | {ledger['fa_ref']} | {date} |"
            f" {total_resolved}/{total_rows} trials ({rate}) | {cost_cell} |"
            f" {ledger['run_url']} |",
        ]
        if compromised_entries:
            # gh-1579/IT-4: the pasted row must never silently include
            # compromised trials — the caveat sits inside the paste block.
            n = len(compromised_entries)
            noun = "trial" if n == 1 else "trials"
            verb = "is" if n == 1 else "are"
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(
                f"gh-1579: {n} verifier-compromised {noun} (verdict untrusted) "
                f"{verb} excluded from the resolution above — do not paste "
                "without the caveat."
            )
    return lines, problems


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("jobs_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-trials", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--family", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--fa-ref", dest="fa_ref", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_url", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    # Issue #1124: key the report to one dataset family — ignore job dirs
    # from other families so merged artifacts never cross-contaminate.
    job_dirs = [d for d in sorted(args.jobs_dir.glob("*")) if d.is_dir()]
    if args.family:
        job_dirs = [d for d in job_dirs if d.name.startswith(f"fa-{args.family}-")]

    splits: dict[str, list[dict]] = {"cpu": [], "gpu": []}
    for job_dir in job_dirs:
        name = job_dir.name
        if "-gpu-" in name:
            split = "gpu"
        elif "-cpu-" in name:
            split = "cpu"
        else:
            # legacy scheme: docker shards were CPU, modal was the GPU leg
            split = "gpu" if "modal" in name else "cpu"
        splits[split].extend(_trial_rows(job_dir))

    # Lazy: only the family path needs the manifest, and importlib-based
    # test harnesses load this module without the dir on sys.path.
    title = ledger = None
    if args.family:
        import families

        if args.family not in families.FAMILIES:
            # Defense in depth: the workflow resolves the dataset via
            # families.py before dispatch, but a direct summary call must
            # not silently render a mis-keyed report.
            print(
                f"::error::unknown Terminal-Bench family '{args.family}' —"
                f" resolve the dataset id first (families.py resolve);"
                f" known: {', '.join(sorted(families.FAMILIES))}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

        title = f"### fa on Terminal-Bench {args.family} ({families.FAMILIES[args.family]})"
        ledger = {
            "dataset": families.FAMILIES[args.family],
            "model": args.model or "—",
            "fa_ref": args.fa_ref or "—",
            "run_url": args.run_url or "—",
        }

    lines, problems = render(
        splits,
        args.expected_trials,
        title=title,
        ledger=ledger,
        run_label=os.environ.get("BENCH_RUN_LABEL", "").strip() or None,
    )

    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"):
        with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    else:
        print("\n".join(lines))

    return 0 if not problems else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1583
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1583
- **Title**: gh-1579 [GOAL] Verifier integrity gate: compromised verifier stdout (skipped browser batches) never counts as resolved — filter-js-from-html false-pass
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1579` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 10
- **Additions**: +1843
- **Deletions**: -8
- **Created**: 2026-10-13T10:14:12Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-13T17:54:11Z

## PR Description

Closes #1579
### What changed

Added the **verifier integrity gate** (gh-1579): `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` now reads each trial's `verifier/test-stdout.txt` and classifies it through the new pure module `bench/harbor_fa/verifier_integrity.py` before the harbor verdict is trusted — a run whose verifier silently skipped work (browser batches that never loaded) becomes `verifier_compromised` and can never count as resolved.

### Key decisions

- **Structured verdict, not a bool**: `classify(stdout) -> IntegrityVerdict{status: ok|suspect|compromised|unreadable, signals, skipped_tests, total_tests}` — signals name *which* batches were skipped; S1 `FailedLoad` (full `HTTPConnectionPool … Read timed out/refused/reset` shape bound to the preceding `RUN BATCH` header, E8/UT-5), S2 `RetryStorm` (≥ `RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD=20` alone → `suspect`, never quarantines — E3), S3 `SuccessClaim` (the `✓ blocked all N` line captured verbatim, a lie marker only when S1 fired — E6).
- **Scoring quarantine (I1)**: compromised scored trials leave the pool entirely — excluded from both the resolved numerator and the clean denominator — and are listed by name: `Verifier-compromised trials (verdict untrusted, excluded from resolution): … (batches 2,5,16,20 skipped — 66/439 vectors never ran) ×1`. Suspect annotates without score change; a pass with missing/undecodable stdout is flagged `verifier_unreadable` (I2, pass-only). Errored-class (gh-1556) and exit-code semantics unchanged (REG-4); legacy no-stdout layouts keep their shape except the unreadable annotation (AC8/REG-3).
- **Fail-closed + bounded**: absent/blank/undecodable/NUL-garbage → `unreadable`, never silently ok; bounded literal+simple-regex line scan — 100 MB parses in ~1s (UT-4 ReDoS bound); report lines quote batch/skip metadata only, never raw stdout (byte-scan test).
- **Golden fixtures** (`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/verifier_integrity/`, deterministic `generate.py`): the `hoBwRwp` incident synthesis (4/28 batches skipped, 66/439 vectors, 84 retries, contradicting claim) + the 4 clean siblings — REG-1/REG-2 are merge-blocking regression pins.
- **Upstream escalation (AC9)**: filed [harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2#89](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2/issues/89) with the fail-or-retry patch shape (draft: `outputs/upstream-issue-filter-js-from-html.md`).

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 117 tests green (26 classifier + 11 gate + 80 existing golden)
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[trial dir verifier/test-stdout.txt] --> R[summary._trial_rows reads + classifies]
  R --> C[verifier_integrity.classify]
  C -->|compromised| Q[excluded from resolved AND clean denominator - named breakdown line]
  C -->|suspect| A[annotation only - score stands]
  C -->|unreadable| F[pass flagged verifier_unreadable]
  C -->|ok| S[scored as before]
```

</details>

Notes: E2E-1 (AC10) is dispatch-gated on the real run-38271607849 artifacts; the committed end-to-end test replays the incident shape through the full pipeline on the pinned fixtures. Pre-existing, unrelated failure on base `b203d3d`: `bench/mls_bench test_build_run.RegressionPinsTest.test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` still pins the pre-#1316 `terminal-bench@4.0.0` default — left untouched for the test-automation owner.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1583._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/verifier_integrity/generate.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: REG-1 pins a synthesis, not the real incident stdout**

The ticket's UT-1/REG-1 (merge-blocking pin) says "real `hoBwRwp` stdout fixture → compromised". This PR commits a **deterministic synthesis** of that artifact (`generate.py` rebuilds the shape from the evidence quoted in the ticket). That is a good auditable negative/positive pair, but a synthesis proves only the synthesis: if the real run-38271607849 stdout differs in any pinned detail (line wrapping of the `Failed to load URL: HTTPConnectionPool … Read timed out` shape, a `\r` carriage return, a port context the regex doesn't cover), REG-1 stays green while the gate misses the actual incident — the exact false-pass this card exists to prevent.

The PR honestly discloses this ("incident synthesis") and E2E-1/AC10 on the real artifacts is explicitly deferred ("optional for merge; required before closing this card"), so this is not merge-blocking — but the gap should be closed before the card is:

1. Download/locate the real `filter-js-from-html__hoBwRwp/verifier/test-stdout.txt` from run 38271607849.
2. Run `classify()` over it (E2E-1) and assert `COMPROMISED`, batches {2,5,16,20}, `skipped_tests == 66`.
3. Pin the real bytes (or a verbatim excerpt preserving the exact failure-line shapes) as an additional fixture next to the synthesis, so REG-1 protects against real-world drift too.

---

### Thread 2 — `bench/harbor_fa/verifier_integrity.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: A `FailedLoad` is permanent — interacts badly with the AC9 upstream retry patch shape**

`seen_batches` records a failed batch id forever; nothing can ever un-signal it. Today that is correct — the incident verifier silently skips a failed batch and never re-runs it. But this PR's own upstream escalation (AC9, terminal-bench-2#89) proposes exactly this patch shape:

> on `Failed to load URL` the test must `pytest.fail(...)` **or retry once with a fresh driver, then fail**

If upstream adopts the retry variant, an honest recovering run would log a second `RUN BATCH N (contains K tests)` header followed by successful vector lines — and this gate would still report `COMPROMISED` (quarantined from resolution) for a batch whose tests *did* all run. That violates the card's own false-positive discipline ("the gate must never remove trust wrongly") for the future world the PR is actively lobbying upstream to create.

Minimal fix now (no detection-logic change required):
- document the one-shot semantics in the `FailedLoad`/`seen_batches` docstring ("a batch that re-runs successfully after a failed load is still flagged — by design until upstream ships a distinguishable retry marker"), and
- pin that decision with a UT (second `RUN BATCH 2` header + success lines after the failure ⇒ still `COMPROMISED`), so a later reviewer knows it is a deliberate contract, not an oversight.

Alternatively, clear the signal for batch N when a later header with the same id is followed by vector-result lines — but then the ticket's E-series needs a new case and the false-positive/false-negative trade should be re-weighed explicitly.

---

### Thread 3 — `bench/harbor_fa/verifier_integrity.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
💡 **SUGGESTION: pre-header (unknown-binding) failures are not deduped**

Batch-bound failures dedup through `seen_batches` ("repeat failures in the same batch count once", per the module docstring), but the E1 branch appends a fresh `FailedLoad(None, None)` for **every** failed-load line seen before any `RUN BATCH` header. A verifier prologue/epilogue with a flapping driver (the incident logged 56 refused + resets) could yield many unknown signals, and `describe()` would render:

```
batches unknown,unknown,unknown,unknown skipped — skipped-test count unknown
```

Dedup unknowns the same way (e.g. a single `has_unknown` flag, or `if not any(s.batch is None for s in loads)` before appending) so the report line stays stable regardless of how many prologue hiccups occurred. Status is unaffected either way — this is report hygiene only.

---

### Thread 4 — `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
💡 **SUGGESTION: ledger caveat counts errored-but-compromised trials too**

`compromised_entries` deliberately includes errored trials with poisoned stdout (E7 — good for post-mortems). But this caveat uses the same list:

```python
n = len(compromised_entries)
```

The sentence claims "N verifier-compromised trials … **are excluded from the resolution above**" — yet an errored-compromised trial was *already* excluded from resolution by the gh-1556 errored class, before the gate saw it. On the E7/REG-4 mixed fixture the caveat overstates its own effect (e.g. claims "2 … are excluded" where only 1 changed pools).

Consider scoring-only counting here (`total_compromised`, already computed — it counts `scored` rows only) while the full breakdown line keeps listing both. The list-comprehension identity is already available; the wording then matches the actual pool delta the caveat warns paste-consumers about.

---

### Thread 5 — `bench/harbor_fa/test_verifier_integrity.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):
💡 **SUGGESTION: wall-clock time-box on a 100 MB parse is a CI flake risk**

```python
self.assertLess(elapsed, 30.0, f"100 MB parse took {elapsed:.1f}s")
```

This is the right *intent* (the ticket mandates a time-boxed ReDoS bound), but a wall-clock assertion in a merge-blocking lane will eventually flake on a loaded or throttled runner: the test builds a ~105 MB string, `splitlines()` materializes ~2.1M line objects (~300+ MB peak), then runs 4 regex searches per line. Locally the whole suite runs in ~6 s, but a 5–10× slower runner eats most of the 30 s headroom.

Cheaper ways to keep the bound pinned without the flake surface:

- shrink the blob to ~10 MB and scale the assertion proportionally (the linear-time *property* is what UT-4 pins; 10 MB still proves it),
- or keep 100 MB but assert a throughput floor (`lines/sec` rather than absolute seconds),
- or mark this one test to run outside the merge-gating lane.

Also consider `sys.intern`-free iteration is already fine — no change needed there; this is purely about the assertion's fragility.

---

### Thread 6 — `bench/harbor_fa/test_verifier_integrity.py`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

# pr-1583: gh-1579 [GOAL] Verifier integrity gate: compromised verifier stdout (skipped browser batches) never counts as resolved — filter-js-from-html false-pass

## Description

Closes #1579
### What changed

Added the **verifier integrity gate** (gh-1579): `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` now reads each trial's `verifier/test-stdout.txt` and classifies it through the new pure module `bench/harbor_fa/verifier_integrity.py` before the harbor verdict is trusted — a run whose verifier silently skipped work (browser batches that never loaded) becomes `verifier_compromised` and can never count as resolved.

### Key decisions

- **Structured verdict, not a bool**: `classify(stdout) -> IntegrityVerdict{status: ok|suspect|compromised|unreadable, signals, skipped_tests, total_tests}` — signals name *which* batches were skipped; S1 `FailedLoad` (full `HTTPConnectionPool … Read timed out/refused/reset` shape bound to the preceding `RUN BATCH` header, E8/UT-5), S2 `RetryStorm` (≥ `RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD=20` alone → `suspect`, never quarantines — E3), S3 `SuccessClaim` (the `✓ blocked all N` line captured verbatim, a lie marker only when S1 fired — E6).
- **Scoring quarantine (I1)**: compromised scored trials leave the pool entirely — excluded from both the resolved numerator and the clean denominator — and are listed by name: `Verifier-compromised trials (verdict untrusted, excluded from resolution): … (batches 2,5,16,20 skipped — 66/439 vectors never ran) ×1`. Suspect annotates without score change; a pass with missing/undecodable stdout is flagged `verifier_unreadable` (I2, pass-only). Errored-class (gh-1556) and exit-code semantics unchanged (REG-4); legacy no-stdout layouts keep their shape except the unreadable annotation (AC8/REG-3).
- **Fail-closed + bounded**: absent/blank/undecodable/NUL-garbage → `unreadable`, never silently ok; bounded literal+simple-regex line scan — 100 MB parses in ~1s (UT-4 ReDoS bound); report lines quote batch/skip metadata only, never raw stdout (byte-scan test).
- **Golden fixtures** (`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/verifier_integrity/`, deterministic `generate.py`): the `hoBwRwp` incident synthesis (4/28 batches skipped, 66/439 vectors, 84 retries, contradicting claim) + the 4 clean siblings — REG-1/REG-2 are merge-blocking regression pins.
- **Upstream escalation (AC9)**: filed [harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2#89](https://github.com/harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2/issues/89) with the fail-or-retry patch shape (draft: `outputs/upstream-issue-filter-js-from-html.md`).

### How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 117 tests green (26 classifier + 11 gate + 80 existing golden)
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T[trial dir verifier/test-stdout.txt] --> R[summary._trial_rows reads + classifies]
  R --> C[verifier_integrity.classify]
  C -->|compromised| Q[excluded from resolved AND clean denominator - named breakdown line]
  C -->|suspect| A[annotation only - score stands]
  C -->|unreadable| F[pass flagged verifier_unreadable]
  C -->|ok| S[scored as before]
```

</details>

Notes: E2E-1 (AC10) is dispatch-gated on the real run-38271607849 artifacts; the committed end-to-end test replays the incident shape through the full pipeline on the pinned fixtures. Pre-existing, unrelated failure on base `b203d3d`: `bench/mls_bench test_build_run.RegressionPinsTest.test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` still pins the pre-#1316 `terminal-bench@4.0.0` default — left untouched for the test-automation owner.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verifier integrity gate (gh-1579) — classify harbor verifier stdout.

A harbor trial's verifier can silently skip work: the filter-js-from-html
verifier drives 439 XSS vectors through a real Chrome in 28 batches, and
when a batch page fails to load (chromedriver read timeout / connection
refused) the batch's vectors are silently skipped and implicitly counted
as blocked — while the test still prints its success claim. The scorer
that only reads `rewards` then trusts a lie.

This module is the named protocol every trust decision about a verifier
verdict passes through: ``classify(stdout_text) -> IntegrityVerdict``.
It is PURE — stdout text in, a structured verdict out, no IO, no eval,
no shell, no template rendering of captured groups (verifier stdout is
task-influenced output: data, never instructions). The file read lives in
``read_stdout`` (called from summary._trial_rows); captured log text is
length-capped before it leaves this module, and report lines built from a
verdict quote only batch/skip metadata, never raw log blobs.

Signals (the core set):

- S1 ``FailedLoad`` — a ``Failed to load URL: HTTPConnectionPool(...):
  Read timed out|Connection refused|ConnectionResetError`` line, bound to
  the preceding ``RUN BATCH N (contains K tests)`` header (batch id +
  skipped-test count). A failure seen before any header binds to no
  batch (batch=None, E1) and contributes 0 to ``skipped_tests``. One
  signal per batch (repeat failures in the same batch count once).
- S2 ``RetryStorm`` — urllib3 ``Retrying (...)`` / ``ConnectionResetError``
  churn. At/above ``RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD`` alone it downgrades the
  verdict to ``suspect`` (annotation only, never a score change); the
  threshold is calibrated above the clean siblings' handful of retries.
- S3 ``SuccessClaim`` — a ``✓ ... blocked all N ...`` summary line
  captured verbatim (length-capped). Only a signal when S1 fired in the
  same stdout (E6): the claim contradicts the failed loads — the lie
  marker. A lone success line is the normal clean case.

Statuses:

- ``ok``          — no S1, S2 below threshold; the verdict stands.
- ``suspect``     — S2 alone at/above threshold; annotated, score stands.
- ``compromised`` — S1 fired; the verdict is untrusted (I1: a trial in
  this state can never count as resolved).
- ``unreadable``  — stdout absent/blank/undecodable (I2: absence of
  evidence is reported, never assumed clean; a pass may still score, but
  the report flags that the gate could not inspect it).

The detector matches patterns, not task names (I3): the same failure mode
in any browser/HTTP-driven verifier of any family is caught. Patterns are
bounded literal+simple-regex matches over a line stream — no nested
quantifiers, no backreferences — so a 100 MB stdout parses in linear
time (UT-4 pins the bound).

Upstream escalation (the task-side fix, fail-or-retry instead of a
silent skip): harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2#89.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

OK = "ok"
SUSPECT = "suspect"
COMPROMISED = "compromised"
UNREADABLE = "unreadable"

# E3: retry/connection churn below this many events leaves the verdict
# ok — the clean sibling trials log a handful of retries and must stay
# quiet; the incident run logged 84. Named constant, pinned by UT-3.
RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD = 20

# Captured log text is length-capped before it enters any verdict/report.
_MAX_CLAIM_CHARS = 200

_BATCH_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"RUN BATCH (\d+) \(contains (\d+) tests\)")
# E8: bound to the full driver-failure shape, never the bare "Failed to
# load URL" substring (a task about error pages must not trip the gate).
_FAILED_LOAD_RE = re.compile(
    r"Failed to load URL: HTTPConnectionPool\([^)]*\): "
    r"(?:Read timed out|Connection refused|ConnectionResetError)"
)
_RETRY_RE = re.compile(r"Retrying \(")
_RESET_RE = re.compile(r"ConnectionResetError")
_CLAIM_RE = re.compile(r"✓.*\bblocked all (\d+)\b")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FailedLoad:
    """S1: a page the verifier failed to load — its tests never ran."""

    batch: int | None  # None = seen before any RUN BATCH header (E1)
    n_tests: int | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RetryStorm:
    """S2: urllib3 retry/connection churn (annotation-grade on its own)."""

    count: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SuccessClaim:
    """S3: the success claim line, verbatim (length-capped) — a lie marker
    only when a FailedLoad fired in the same stdout (E6)."""

    claim: str
    total_tests: int | None


Signal = FailedLoad | RetryStorm | SuccessClaim


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IntegrityVerdict:
    """The structured trust verdict for one verifier stdout."""

    status: str  # OK | SUSPECT | COMPROMISED | UNREADABLE
    signals: tuple[Signal, ...]
    skipped_tests: int | None  # batch-bound skips; None when no S1 fired
    total_tests: int | None = None  # claimed/header-declared vector total

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """Report-grade detail: batches + skip counts only — never raw log
        text (report lines quote metadata, not blobs)."""
        loads = [s for s in self.signals if isinstance(s, FailedLoad)]
        batches = [
            "unknown" if s.batch is None else str(s.batch) for s in loads
        ]
        batch_part = f"batches {','.join(batches)} skipped"
        skips = self.skipped_tests or 0
        if skips and self.total_tests:
            skip_part = f"{skips}/{self.total_tests} vectors never ran"
        elif skips:
            skip_part = f"{skips} vectors never ran"
        else:
            # Unknown-bindings contribute 0 (E1): no attributable skips.
            skip_part = "skipped-test count unknown"
        return f"{batch_part} — {skip_part}"


def classify(stdout_text: str | None) -> IntegrityVerdict:
    """Classify one verifier's stdout (pure; None = absent/undecodable)."""
    if stdout_text is None or "\x00" in stdout_text or not stdout_text.strip():
        # I2, fail-closed: absent, blank, or binary garbage is unreadable —
        # never silently ok on a pass.
        return IntegrityVerdict(UNREADABLE, (), None, None)

    loads: list[FailedLoad] = []
    seen_batches: set[int] = set()
    current: tuple[int, int] | None = None  # (batch id, n tests)
    retry_count = 0
    claim: SuccessClaim | None = None
    header_total = 0

    for line in stdout_text.splitlines():
        header = _BATCH_HEADER_RE.search(line)
        if header:
            current = (int(header.group(1)), int(header.group(2)))
            header_total += current[1]
            continue
        if _FAILED_LOAD_RE.search(line):
            if current is None:
                # E1: outside any batch — kept, but never misattributed.
                loads.append(FailedLoad(None, None))
            elif current[0] not in seen_batches:
                loads.append(FailedLoad(current[0], current[1]))
                seen_batches.add(current[0])
            continue
        if _RETRY_RE.search(line) or _RESET_RE.search(line):
            retry_count += 1
            continue
        if claim is None:
            match = _CLAIM_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                claim = SuccessClaim(
                    line.strip()[:_MAX_CLAIM_CHARS], int(match.group(1))
                )

    signals: list[Signal] = list(loads)
    skipped_tests: int | None = None
    total_tests: int | None = None
    if loads:
        skipped_tests = sum(s.n_tests or 0 for s in loads if s.batch is not None)
        total_tests = claim.total_tests if claim else (header_total or None)
        if claim is not None:
            signals.append(claim)  # S3 requires S1 (E6)
    elif claim is not None:
        total_tests = claim.total_tests
    if retry_count >= RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD:
        signals.append(RetryStorm(retry_count))

    if loads:
        status = COMPROMISED
    elif retry_count >= RETRY_STORM_THRESHOLD:
        status = SUSPECT
    else:
        status = OK
    return IntegrityVerdict(status, tuple(signals), skipped_tests, total_tests)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resolution-rate summary for harbor job dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--expected-trials N] <jobs-dir>

Reads <jobs-dir>/<job>/*/result.json (per-trial TrialResults; each job's
top-level result.json is a file, not a dir, so the glob skips it) and
prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown resolution table, also appending it to
$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): each trial's fa session usage is folded
into result.json's agent_result by fa_agent.py (n_input/n_output/
n_cache_tokens, estimated share in metadata, cost_usd derived from the
pinned bench price table bench/pricing.json — null renders n/a, never a
made-up price). The table gains per-split tokens/cost columns next to the
resolution rate; a spend line carries the overall totals.

Jobs named fa-4.0-<env>-gpu-<shard> count as the GPU split; everything
else is CPU (bench-harbor.yml names jobs fa-<family>-<env>-<kind>-<shard>;
the legacy fa-4.0-{docker,modal}-<shard> names map modal -> GPU).

--family (issue #1124) keys the report to one Terminal-Bench dataset
family: job dirs from OTHER families are ignored — merged artifacts from
different dataset versions never cross-contaminate a report — and the
report ends in a paste-ready row for the per-version results ledger in
docs/bench.md (dataset, model, fa commit, date, resolution, cost, run —
cost from the same pricing.json accounting, n/a when unpriced). Without
--family the legacy behaviour applies (all job dirs; title pinned to 4.0;
no ledger block).

A trial is resolved when every verifier reward is 1.0; the resolution rate
is resolved trials / scored (non-errored) trials. gh-1579 adds the
verifier integrity gate: every trial's verifier stdout
(verifier/test-stdout.txt) is classified by verifier_integrity.classify()
before the verdict is trusted — a trial whose verifier silently skipped
work (browser batches that never loaded) is `verifier_compromised`, a
fourth reported-only class: pulled out of the scored pool entirely
(neither resolved numerator nor clean denominator — I1), listed by name
in its own breakdown line. Retry/connection storms without failed loads
are `suspect` — annotated, score unchanged. A pass whose verifier stdout
is missing or undecodable is flagged `verifier_unreadable` (I2: absence
of evidence is reported, never assumed clean). Legacy layouts without
verifier stdout keep their shape except the unreadable annotation; the
errored-class (gh-1556) and exit-code semantics are unchanged — the gate
reports, it never reddens the step.

harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials, so the exit code is the
verdict on run COMPLETENESS
only: 1 when nothing was produced or fewer than --expected-trials trials
produced a readable result.json (lost shard). gh-1556 AC3: the
completeness count is by PRESENCE — a trial whose result.json was written
counts as attempted regardless of exception class, so legitimate
dataset-cap or ladder timeouts (errored before a verdict) can never redden
the job; the errored class gets its own breakdown line instead, and exit 1
is reserved for genuinely lost trials. Unresolved trials are the
scoreboard, not an infra failure — reported without failing the step.
"""
import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def _ledger_records(trial_dir: Path) -> list:
    """Every hidden `task_ledger` custom record in the trial's synced fa
    session logs, in file then line order."""
    ledgers = []
    for sessions in sorted(trial_dir.glob("agent*/fah-sessions")):
        for path in sorted(sessions.glob("*.jsonl")):
            try:
                text = path.read_text()
            except OSError:
                continue
            for line in text.splitlines():
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    record = json.loads(line)
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue
                if (
                    isinstance(record, dict)
                    and record.get("type") == "custom"
                    and record.get("customType") == "task_ledger"
                ):
                    ledgers.append(record)
    return ledgers


_LEDGER_VERIFIED = ("pass", "fixed")  # keep in lockstep with the Dart
# `TaskLedgerItemStatus` enum and the SIBLING copy in
# bench/terminal_bench/summary.py (the two summary scripts are
# standalone-by-design — different layout roots — so this parser is
# duplicated; change both together).


def _ledger_cell(trial_dir: Path) -> str:
    """gh-1412: the trial's checklist-coverage cell from its last hidden
    `task_ledger` record — "checklist: V/T [(N unmet)]", "checklist: none"
    when the session carries no ledger.

    Tolerates the corrupt payloads the Dart fold deliberately tolerates
    ("a corrupt ledger payload never throws"): a non-dict `data`, or an
    `items` that is not a list, degrades to `checklist: none` — never an
    AttributeError. An items-less ledger is `none` too: it verifies
    nothing, and rendering 0/0 would count it as fully verified in the
    coverage tally below. Duplicate of the sibling parser in
    bench/terminal_bench/summary.py (the scripts are standalone-by-design)
    — change both together.
    """
    ledgers = _ledger_records(trial_dir)
    if not ledgers:
        return "checklist: none"
    data = ledgers[-1].get("data")
    rows = data.get("items") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    items = rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []
    if not items:
        return "checklist: none"
    total = len(items)
    verified = sum(
        1
        for item in items
        if isinstance(item, dict)
        and str(item.get("status") or "").lower() in _LEDGER_VERIFIED
    )
    unmet = total - verified
    cell = f"checklist: {verified}/{total}"
    if unmet:
        cell += f" ({unmet} unmet)"
    return cell


def _status(row: dict) -> str:
    """The row's integrity status (gh-1579). Rows that predate the gate
    (hand-built splits) count as ok — the gate is additive (AC8)."""
    verdict = row.get("integrity")
    return verdict.status if verdict is not None else "ok"


def _trial_rows(job_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
    # gh-1579: the integrity gate rides the same lazy-import pattern as
    # families below — importlib-based harnesses load this module
    # without this dir on sys.path.
    import verifier_integrity as vi

    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(str(job_dir / "*" / "result.json"))):
        data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
        rewards = (data.get("verifier_result") or {}).get("rewards") or {}
        scores = [float(v) for v in rewards.values()]
        resolved = bool(scores) and all(v >= 1.0 for v in scores)
        exception = (data.get("exception_info") or {}).get("exception_type") or ""
        # Issue #1123: token/cost accounting folded in by fa_agent.py at
        # populate_context_post_run time; absent (old runs) → zeros + n/a.
        agent = data.get("agent_result") or {}
        metadata = agent.get("metadata") or {}
        trial_dir = Path(path).parent
        # gh-1579 integrity gate: read + classify the verifier's stdout
        # BEFORE the verdict is trusted (pure classifier; IO here).
        stdout_text, stdout_reason = vi.read_stdout(trial_dir)
        verdict = vi.classify(stdout_text)
        if verdict.status == vi.COMPROMISED:
            note = verdict.describe()
        elif verdict.status == vi.SUSPECT:
            storms = [
                s.count for s in verdict.signals if isinstance(s, vi.RetryStorm)
            ]
            note = f"{storms[0]} retry/connection warnings"
        elif verdict.status == vi.UNREADABLE:
            note = f"stdout {stdout_reason}"
        else:
            note = ""
        rows.append({
            "resolved": resolved,
            "exception": exception,
            "tokens_in": agent.get("n_input_tokens") or 0,
            "tokens_out": agent.get("n_output_tokens") or 0,
            "cost": agent.get("cost_usd"),
            "estimated": metadata.get("estimated_tokens") or 0,
   …
